questions.prompt: A student writes "help with exams" and receives a vague plan. Which prompt revision is most useful?

options.a: Specify exam subjects, available days, format and measurable revision tasks
options.b: Request a longer answer without supplying any goals
options.c: Ask the assistant to predict exact exam questions

questions.feedback: Useful prompts contain a concrete outcome, relevant facts, constraints and acceptance checks.

questions.prompt: A bookshop writes "make marketing" and receives generic text. Which follow-up is best?

options.a: Request guaranteed sales with invented endorsements
options.b: Give only the shop name and request an immediate final campaign
options.c: Name the product, buyer, verified features and required caption length

questions.feedback: Useful prompts contain a concrete outcome, relevant facts, constraints and acceptance checks.

questions.prompt: A volunteer wants help summarizing a roster with actual phone numbers. Which input is suitable for a public tool?

options.a: Paste the full contact database for realism
options.b: Include passwords to avoid further clarification
options.c: Use an authorized minimized or fictional roster with no unnecessary identifiers

questions.feedback: Use minimal authorized input and keep actual identifiers outside unapproved tools.

questions.prompt: A freelancer is drafting a sample invoice that contains a real client's bank details. Which test data is appropriate?

options.a: Share an open folder of customer invoices
options.b: Replace personal account fields with synthetic placeholders before testing
options.c: Post the original financial identifiers in the prompt

questions.feedback: Use minimal authorized input and keep actual identifiers outside unapproved tools.

questions.prompt: An AI supplies a study citation without any verifiable publication record. Which next step is appropriate?

options.a: Invent a matching DOI to make the source look real
options.b: Withhold the citation until a reliable independent source confirms it
options.c: Trust the publication title because it sounds academic

questions.feedback: Model fluency cannot substitute for independent factual verification.

questions.prompt: A generated course summary gives an application deadline but cites no date or source. What should happen?

options.a: Verify the deadline on the responsible official website and record the date checked
options.b: Assume that last year's deadline remains valid
options.c: Publish the claim as certain because it was fluently phrased

questions.feedback: Model fluency cannot substitute for independent factual verification.

questions.prompt: Two prompts write plans for the same learner. What makes the evaluation fair?

options.a: Use identical learner constraints and score both outputs against one rubric
options.b: Give them different goals and compare only length
options.c: Select the version with the most polished adjectives

questions.feedback: Consistent inputs and criteria make comparisons interpretable; edge cases need testing.

questions.prompt: Two customer-support response templates are compared before rollout. Which approach is defensible?

options.a: Use unrelated cases with different severity and compare tone alone
options.b: Treat the first valid output as proof of universal reliability
options.c: Test both on the same fictional ticket set for accuracy, clarity and policy fit

questions.feedback: Consistent inputs and criteria make comparisons interpretable; edge cases need testing.
